answer.rationale: The mandate requires an 18% cut the incumbent won't offer, and the low-cost vendor's quote meets it (memory_c2 shows their onboarding and invoicing held up). But the line runs at 94% with zero buffer and the contract lapses in 14 days, so a full switch creates an unmitigated single point of failure. Memory_c3 shows a second source removed exactly this failure mode during a shortage. Adding the low-cost vendor as a qualified second source with a guarded initial allocation captures partial savings this cycle, preserves incumbent supply through the gap, and builds the leverage for a full shift or renegotiation at the next review. Verifying c3 before committing since the whole plan hinges on dual-sourcing having actually held up.
